definition_zh: 防水的；不透水的；防水材料；使防水
definition_en: not letting water through, and to treat something so that water cannot pass
core_image: 雨衣上一颗水珠滚成一粒圆球，滑下去，衣面还是干的
scene: 山顶忽然下起雨，别人都在找地方躲，他把帽子一压，外套上全是滚落的水珠。 Take a waterproof; the forecast is bad.
sceneCN: 这里 waterproof 是「防水的」（第 1 个义项：水透不过去）；句意为带件雨衣吧，预报说天气不好。雨衣上滚落的水珠就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ing 构成，义为「防水处理；防水材料」
过去分词作形容词，义为「做过防水处理的」
近义复合词，义为「抗水的」
近义复合词，义为「不透水的；严密的」

senses.title: Not letting water through
senses.definition: made or treated so that water cannot pass through
senses.definitionCN: 经过制作或处理，使水无法透过
senses.example: These boots are waterproof enough for crossing the stream.
senses.exampleCN: 这双靴子防水够好，可以蹚过小溪。
senses.why: Water plus proof, in the old sense of proof meaning «able to resist», gives exactly «no water gets through».
senses.whyCN: water 加上 proof（古义为「能抵御」），正好得出「水进不去」。

senses.title: A waterproof garment
senses.definition: a coat or other garment made of waterproof material, often called waterproofs in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 用防水材料制成的外套等，常用复数 waterproofs 指整套防水衣物
senses.example: Pack your waterproofs before you set off.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前把防水衣物装好。
senses.why: When the adjective is used so often with one kind of clothing, the adjective becomes the name of that clothing.
senses.whyCN: 当形容词常与某一类衣物连用时，形容词本身就变成了这类衣物的名字。

senses.title: To treat with a waterproof coating
senses.definition: to put a substance on something so that water cannot get in
senses.definitionCN: 在物体上涂敷物质，使水无法渗入
senses.example: They waterproofed the roof before the rainy season.
senses.exampleCN: 雨季之前他们给屋顶做了防水。
senses.why: Making an object waterproof is a job, so the adjective took a verb form: to waterproof something.
senses.whyCN: 让物体防水是一项工作，因此这个形容词也有了动词形式：to waterproof。

senses.title: Of things seen as roughly water-safe
senses.definition: in product labels, said of watches and phones that survive contact with water, though often not deep diving
senses.definitionCN: 在商品标识中形容手表、手机等不怕接触水，但通常并非深潜可用
senses.example: The watch is waterproof to fifty metres.
senses.exampleCN: 这只手表防水深度五十米。
senses.why: Labels need a short, strong word, so waterproof was stretched to cover everything from ink to watches, with a stated depth.
senses.whyCN: 标签需要一个简短有力的词，于是 waterproof 被扩展到从墨水到手表，再附上一个标注深度。

intro.en: Waterproof is an English compound of water and proof, where proof keeps its old sense of «able to resist».
intro.cn: waterproof 由 water 与 proof 合成的英语复合词，其中 proof 保留着「能抵御」的古义。

items.en: Proof comes from the Latin probare through Old French, and first meant the act of testing.
items.cn: proof 经古法语来自拉丁语 probare，最初指「检验」这一行为。

items.en: From testing, proof came to mean tried and found good, and then able to resist, as in fireproof.
items.cn: 由检验引申出「经过试验而可靠」，再引申为「能抵御」，如 fireproof。

items.en: Water and proof were joined in the eighteenth century to describe cloth that rain could not pass.
items.cn: 十八世纪 water 与 proof 合成一词，用来形容雨透不过的布料。

items.en: Vulcanised rubber and waxed cloth made waterproofing a trade, with its own craftsmen.
items.cn: 硫化橡胶与蜡布使防水处理成为一门有专门匠人的行业。

items.en: The word now labels watches, phones and mascara, always with an implied «how deep» or «how long».
items.cn: 如今这词标在手电、手机与睫毛膏上，总暗含「多深」或「多久」。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on waterproof and its near partners, the second the related -proof compounds and resistance words.
note.cn: 第一组收 waterproof 的派生与近邻词，第二组收同类 -proof 复合词与表示抵挡的词。

entries.definition: Plural noun and third person singular.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数与第三人称单数

entries.definition: Past tense and participle, also an adjective.

entries.definition: The noun for the treatment itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指防水处理本身的名词

entries.definition: Closed so tightly that no water can enter at all.
Resists water but is not fully proof against it.
The garment most often called waterproof.
entries.definitionCN: 雨衣，最常被称作 waterproof 的衣物

entries.definition: The same -proof pattern, but against fire.
entries.definitionCN: 同样的 -proof 构法，只是防的是火

entries.definition: Not allowing liquid to pass, a formal word.

normalIntro.en: Water plus proof: proof here is not evidence but resistance, as in fireproof and soundproof.
normalIntro.cn: water 加 proof：这里的 proof 不是「证据」而是「抵御」，正如 fireproof、soundproof。

normal.en: Proof means proof against, not proof of.
normal.cn: 这里的 proof 是「防住」，不是「证明」。

normal.en: Waterproof is total; water-resistant only resists.
normal.cn: waterproof 是全防，water-resistant 只是抗。

normal.en: Waterproofs as a plural noun means the rain clothes you pack.
normal.cn: 复数名词 waterproofs 指打包带的雨具。

normal.en: The verb keeps the same spelling: to waterproof a roof.
normal.cn: 动词拼写不变：to waterproof a roof。

normal.en: Watertight is stronger still: nothing gets in at all.
normal.cn: watertight 更强：一点都进不去。

abstract.en: Picture round drops rolling off a sleeve.
abstract.cn: 想圆滚滚的水珠从衣袖上滚下。

abstract.en: Hear rain drumming and nothing reaching your skin.
abstract.cn: 听雨点敲打，却一丝没透到身上。

abstract.en: See a label: waterproof to fifty metres.
abstract.cn: 想标签上写着：防水五十米。

examples.en: You will need a waterproof coat for the hills.
examples.cn: 上山你需要一件防水外套。

examples.en: The tent is waterproof but the seams are not.
examples.cn: 帐篷是防水的，但接缝不是。

examples.en: They waterproofed the boots before the trip.
examples.cn: 出发前他们给靴子做了防水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沃特普鲁夫」——沃特普鲁夫站在雨里，衣服上的水珠一颗颗滚下去，里面却干得能摊开报纸。

root: water（水）+ proof（古义「能抵御」），为十八世纪英语复合词。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective comes first, then the garment it names, then the verb of treating something, and finally its use on product labels.
sensesIntro.cn: 先讲形容词，再讲它命名的衣物，然后是做处理的动词，最后是它在商品标签上的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop beading up and rolling off a sleeve.
core.cn: 核心意象：在衣袖上聚成珠、滚下去的一滴水。

branches.en: The material branch: boots that cross a stream.
branches.cn: 材料分支：能蹚过小溪的靴子。

branches.en: The clothing branch: waterproofs packed for the trip.
branches.cn: 衣物分支：为出行打包的雨具。

branches.en: The treating branch: a roof sealed for the rains.
branches.cn: 处理分支：为雨季封好的屋顶。

branches.en: The label branch: a watch rated to fifty metres.
branches.cn: 标签分支：标称五十米的手表。

branches.en: The trade branch: waxed cloth and waterproofing craft.
branches.cn: 行业分支：蜡布与防水手艺。

intro.en: Waterproof joins two free words and then takes -s, -ed and -ing like any verb; -ial words such as impermeable are its formal relatives.
intro.cn: waterproof 由两个自由词合成，再像普通动词一样加 -s、-ed、-ing；impermeable 一类正式词是它的远亲。

latinIntro.en: The element proof entered English through Old French from Latin probare, to test, which is where its sense of resistance grew.
latinIntro.cn: 构件 proof 经古法语来自拉丁语 probare（检验），「抵御」之义正是在那里长出来的。

definition_zh: 抽象的；抽象作品；摘要；提取
definition_en: existing as an idea rather than a physical thing, or a short summary
core_image: 一幅只画了几何色块的画
scene: 美术馆里，一幅没有具体形象的画让人停下来看。 The gallery showed an abstract painting with no clear subject.
sceneCN: 这里的 abstract 指「抽象的」（第 1 个义项：不以具体形象呈现）；句意是美术馆展出一幅没有明确主题的抽象画。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ion 构成，义为「抽象；抽象概念」
义为「出神的；心不在焉的」

senses.title: Not concrete
senses.definition: existing as an idea, not as a physical object
senses.definitionCN: 作为观念而存在，而非具体物体
senses.example: The gallery showed an abstract painting with no clear subject.
senses.exampleCN: 美术馆展出一幅没有明确主题的抽象画。
senses.why: The Latin participle means drawn away, and an idea drawn away from things is abstract.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词意为「被抽走」，从具体事物中抽出的观念就是抽象的。

senses.title: Abstract art
senses.definition: art that does not try to show real objects
senses.definitionCN: 不试图表现真实物体的艺术
senses.example: She prefers abstract to landscape painting.
senses.exampleCN: 比起风景画，她更喜欢抽象画。
senses.why: Art that draws away from likeness keeps the word for what has been removed.
senses.whyCN: 从形似中抽离的艺术，保留了这个「被抽走」的词。

senses.title: A summary
senses.definition: a short account of the main points of a paper
senses.definitionCN: 对论文要点的简短陈述
senses.example: Read the abstract before the full paper.
senses.exampleCN: 先读摘要，再读全文。
senses.why: A summary draws the essence out of a longer text.
senses.whyCN: 摘要就是把要点从长文中抽出来。

senses.title: To extract
senses.definition: takes something out of a larger mass
senses.definitionCN: 从较大的整体中取出某物
senses.example: The process abstracts metal from ore.
senses.exampleCN: 这道工序从矿石中提取金属。
senses.why: The literal sense of drawing away survives in chemistry and mining.
senses.whyCN: 「抽走」的字面义在化学与采矿中留存。

senses.title: In the abstract
senses.definition: in the phrase in the abstract, considered apart from real cases
senses.definitionCN: 在 in the abstract 中，指脱离具体事例来考虑
senses.example: In the abstract, the plan sounds fair.
senses.exampleCN: 从理论上说，这个计划听起来很公平。
senses.why: To consider apart from cases is to draw the idea away from them.
senses.whyCN: 脱离事例来考虑，就是把观念从事例中抽走。

senses.title: An abstract noun
senses.definition: a noun naming a quality or state rather than a thing
senses.definitionCN: 指称性质或状态而非物体的名词
senses.example: Freedom is an abstract noun.
senses.exampleCN: 自由是一个抽象名词。
senses.why: Grammar classifies words by whether they name something drawn away from matter.
senses.whyCN: 语法按是否指称脱离物质之物来分类名词。

senses.title: Lost in thought
senses.definition: in abstracted, with the mind drawn away from the present
senses.definitionCN: 在 abstracted 中，指心思离开了眼前
senses.example: He gave an abstracted reply and walked on.
senses.exampleCN: 他心不在焉地答了一句，继续往前走。
senses.why: A mind drawn away from the room is literally abstracted.
senses.whyCN: 心思被抽离房间，字面上就是被抽走。

senses.title: To remove in chemistry
senses.definition: in chemistry, separates a substance from a mixture
senses.definitionCN: 化学上从混合物中分离出某种物质
senses.example: The lab abstracts the active compound from the leaf.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室从叶子中萃取活性成分。
senses.why: Chemical extraction is the modern technical heir of drawing something out.
senses.whyCN: 化学萃取正是「把某物抽出」的现代技术后裔。

definition_en: a thick roll of tobacco leaves made for smoking, or the cured leaf tobacco used to make it
core_image: 两根手指夹着一支粗大的褐色烟卷
scene: 阳台上有人靠着栏杆，烟雾慢慢散开。 He lit a cigar and watched the harbour.

senses.title: A roll of tobacco leaf
senses.definition: a thick roll of whole tobacco leaves made for smoking
senses.definitionCN: 用整片烟叶卷成、供吸食的粗烟
senses.example: He lit a cigar after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他饭后点了一支雪茄。
senses.why: Spanish cigarro first named a rolled bundle of tobacco leaves.
senses.whyCN: 西班牙语 cigarro 最初指卷起来的一捆烟叶。

senses.title: Leaf tobacco for cigars
senses.definition: the cured leaf tobacco used to make cigars
senses.definitionCN: 用于制作雪茄的晾制烟叶
senses.example: The valley grows tobacco for cigars.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷种植制作雪茄用的烟叶。
senses.why: The raw leaf and the finished roll shared one name in the trade.
senses.whyCN: 在行业里，原料烟叶与卷好的成品共用一个名称。

items.en: Sicar referred to smoking rolled tobacco leaves.

items.en: Cigare carried the word into French salons.

items.en: English cigar kept the thicker final r sound.

definition_en: a small house, especially at the gate of a park or estate; to stay in a place as a paying guest; to make a formal statement to an authority; to become fixed in one position

scene: 山道尽头有一栋矮小的木屋，是守林人夜里落脚的地方。 The keeper went back to his lodge before the snow closed the road.
sceneCN: 这里是「守林人居住的小屋」（第 1 个义项：山地或园林旁供人居住的小房子）；句意为在大雪封路之前，守林人回到了他的小屋。

senses.title: A small house that gives shelter
senses.titleCN: 小屋；门房；园林中的居所
senses.definition: a small house, especially one at the gate of a park or estate, or one used for hunting and short stays
senses.definitionCN: 尤指公园或庄园门口的、或供狩猎和短期居住的小房子
senses.example: The gatekeeper lives in a stone lodge at the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 守门人住在入口处一间石头门房里。
senses.why: Old French loge first meant an arbour or a leafy shelter, so the word names a modest building built to give cover rather than comfort.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 loge 最初指凉棚或用枝叶搭起的遮蔽处，所以这个词命名的是为遮风挡雨而建的简陋房子，不是讲究的住宅。

senses.title: To stay as a paying guest
senses.definition: to stay in someone else's house or in a rented room, usually paying for it
senses.definitionCN: 住在别人家里或租来的房间里，通常需要付费
senses.example: Two students lodged with a family near the campus.
senses.exampleCN: 两名学生寄宿在校园附近的一户人家里。
senses.why: The French verb logier meant to put someone under a roof, and English turned that shelter into an arrangement you pay for, so the noun grew a verb of living.
senses.whyCN: 法语动词 logier 意为把人安置到屋顶之下，英语把这层「安置」变成了付费的居住安排，名词于是长出「寄宿」的动词义。

senses.title: To make a formal statement to an authority
senses.definition: to submit a complaint, appeal or claim officially to a court, council or other authority
senses.definitionCN: 向法院、委员会或其他机构正式提交投诉、上诉或索赔
senses.example: The neighbours lodged a complaint about the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们就噪音问题提出了投诉。
senses.why: The image shifts from a hut to a slot: a document is placed into the proper office the way a parcel is placed in a room, and it stays there as a record.
senses.whyCN: 意象从小屋转到「放入」：文件被放进相应的部门，就像包裹放进一间屋子，并且留在那里成为记录，这就是「正式提出」。

senses.title: To become fixed in one position
senses.definition: to become firmly stuck in a place, or to put something there so that it stays
senses.definitionCN: 牢牢卡在某个位置，或把某物放在那里不再移动
senses.example: A bullet lodged in the wall above the door.
senses.exampleCN: 一颗子弹嵌在门上方的那面墙里。
senses.why: The idea of finding a room extends to objects: whatever settles into a spot and cannot easily move has lodged there, as if it had taken shelter.
senses.whyCN: 「找到一间屋子」的想法延伸到物体：凡是落进某处、不容易再移动的东西，都算 lodged，仿佛它也在那里躲了起来。

intro.en: Lodge came into English from Old French, where a leafy arbour had already become a small building and a verb meaning to shelter someone.
intro.cn: lodge 经古法语进入英语；在法语里，用枝叶搭的凉棚已经变成小建筑，并且有了「安置、留宿」的动词用法。

items.en: Laubia or lobia named a covered gallery or arbour, probably borrowed from a Germanic word for a shelter of leaves.
items.cn: laubia 或 lobia 指带顶的回廊或凉棚，一般认为借自日耳曼语中表示「枝叶搭的遮蔽物」的词。

items.en: Loge meant a hut, arbour or small shelter, and it kept the picture of something built cheaply to give cover.
items.cn: loge 意为小屋、凉棚、简陋的遮蔽处，仍保留「临时搭建、只为遮风挡雨」的画面。

items.en: The verb logier meant to give someone lodging or to stay in a place, and it carried the word into English use.
items.cn: 动词 logier 意为给某人提供住处或自己住在某处，把这个词带入英语的日常使用。

items.en: Middle English lodgen covered both staying in a place and putting something down in a fixed spot.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lodgen 同时指「在某处住下」和「把东西放在固定位置」。

items.en: Modern English adds the legal sense of filing a complaint, and keeps lodger, lodging and dislodge in everyday use.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「正式提交投诉」这一法律义，并让 lodger、lodging、dislodge 留在日常用语里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same French shelter; the near-meaning group gathers other names for small buildings and for staying somewhere.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一个法语「遮蔽处」之上的词；近义组收其他表示小建筑和居住的词。

entries.definition: A person who pays to live in someone else's house.

A place giving protection from weather or danger.

normalIntro.en: Lodge keeps one picture behind all its senses: something is given a place to stay, whether that is a person, a document or a bullet.
normalIntro.cn: lodge 的所有义项背后是同一个画面：一样东西被安置到一个能停留的位置，无论那是人、文件还是子弹。

normal.en: Lodge comes from Old French loge, a leafy arbour, so the first thing it names is a cheap shelter rather than a fine house.
normal.cn: lodge 来自古法语 loge，本指枝叶搭的凉棚，所以它最先命名的是简陋的遮蔽处，而不是好房子。

normal.en: Lodger adds -er to lodge: the person who lives in the little shelter and pays for it.
normal.cn: lodger 在 lodge 后加 -er：住进这间小屋并且付钱的人，就是房客。

normal.en: To lodge a complaint is to put the paper into the right office, the way a parcel is put into a room.
normal.cn: lodge a complaint 是把那份纸放进对应的部门，就像把包裹放进一间屋子。

normal.en: Dislodge takes dis-, meaning away, and drives the thing out of the spot it had settled in.
normal.cn: dislodge 用表示「离开」的 dis-，把已经安顿下来的东西赶出原来的位置。

normal.en: Loggia is a cousin from the same Latin gallery, and it still means a roofed open walkway.
normal.cn: loggia 是同出一个拉丁「回廊」词的亲戚，至今仍指带顶的开放走道。

abstract.en: A hut, a rented room and a bullet in a wall are the same sentence: something has found a place where it can stay.
abstract.cn: 小屋、租来的房间、嵌在墙里的子弹说的是同一句话：某样东西找到了可以停留的位置。

abstract.en: A complaint filed at a counter looks like a quiet act, but the paper stays in the building long after the person leaves.
abstract.cn: 在柜台递出的投诉看上去很安静，但人走了很久以后，那张纸还留在楼里。

abstract.en: The lamp in the gatehouse window is the warmest version of this word: shelter offered before anyone asks.
abstract.cn: 门房窗口那盏灯是这个词最温暖的版本：在有人开口之前就先给出一处遮蔽。

examples.en: A stray bullet lodged in the wall.

examples.en: She lodged with a local family while studying abroad.

examples.en: The residents lodged a complaint about the noise.

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a small shelter; from it come paying lodging, the legal act of placing a complaint, and anything that settles firmly in place.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是遮风挡雨的小屋；由此长出付费寄宿、把投诉正式放入案卷，以及任何牢牢停在原处的东西。

scene: 见面会上两个人同时伸出手。 She smiled awkwardly and stepped back.
sceneCN: 这里 awkwardly 是「尴尬地」（第 1 个义项：带着不自在的神情或方式）；句意是她尴尬地笑了笑，往后退了一步。

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「尴尬的；笨拙的」，awkwardly 由其加 -ly 构成
由 awkward 加 -ness 构成，义为「尴尬；笨拙」

senses.title: With embarrassment
senses.definition: in a way that shows embarrassment
senses.definitionCN: 以显出难为情的方式
senses.example: She smiled awkwardly and stepped back.
senses.exampleCN: 她尴尬地笑了笑，往后退了一步。
senses.why: Awkwardly is awkward plus -ly, and the adverb keeps the social sense of a person out of place.
senses.whyCN: awkwardly 是 awkward 加 -ly，副词保留了人「不合位」时的社交含义。

senses.title: In a clumsy way
senses.definition: in a way that lacks skill or grace
senses.definitionCN: 以缺乏技巧或优雅的方式
senses.example: He climbed awkwardly over the low wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他笨手笨脚地翻过那道矮墙。
senses.why: The physical sense of facing the wrong way produces movements that look stiff and unplanned, which is the second sense of the adverb.
senses.whyCN: 身体朝向不对，动作就显得僵硬、没有章法，这就是副词的第二个义项。

intro.en: Awkwardly carries the wrong-angle image into the adverb.
intro.cn: awkwardly 把「角度不对」的意象带进了副词。

items.en: afugr meant 'turned the wrong way'.
items.cn: afugr 意为「方向转反的」。

items.en: afugligr meant 'unfavourable'.
items.cn: afugligr 意为「不顺的」。

items.en: aukeward meant 'backhanded'.
items.cn: aukeward 意为「反手的」。

items.en: awkwardly meant 'in a clumsy way'.
items.cn: awkwardly 意为「以笨拙的方式」。

items.en: It also describes social discomfort.
items.cn: 如今也描述社交上的不自在。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the aw sound; the near-meaning group gives manner adverbs of unease.
note.cn: 形近组都含 aw 音；近义组是表示不自在的方式副词。

normalIntro.en: Awkwardly is the way a body moves when it has no right angle to stand on.
normalIntro.cn: awkwardly 是身体找不到合适角度时的动法。

normal.en: Awkwardly usually follows a verb of movement or speech.
normal.cn: awkwardly 常跟在表示动作或说话的动词后。

normal.en: The adjective is awkward, without the -ly.
normal.cn: 形容词是 awkward，不带 -ly。

normal.en: Awkwardly phrased means the wording feels unnatural.
normal.cn: awkwardly phrased 指措辞不自然。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AWK-ward-ly.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with awfully, which means very.
normal.cn: 别与表示「非常」的 awfully 混淆。

abstract.en: See two hands offered in the wrong direction.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手朝错的方向伸出。

abstract.en: See a foot catching on a low step.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚被矮台阶绊住。

abstract.en: See a person laughing a beat too late.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人慢半拍才笑出来。

examples.en: She smiled awkwardly and stepped back.
examples.cn: 她尴尬地笑了笑，往后退了一步。

examples.en: He climbed awkwardly over the low wall.
examples.cn: 他笨手笨脚地翻过那道矮墙。

examples.en: The sentence was awkwardly phrased.
examples.cn: 这个句子措辞很别扭。

dict_mnemonic.text: awkward 加 -ly：方向别扭，动作和神情就都跟着不自然。

root: 由 awkward 加 -ly 构成；awkward 来自古诺斯语 afugr「方向转反的」；由「方向不对」引申为尴尬地与笨拙地。

sensesIntro.cn: 社交上的不自在与身体上的笨拙，是同一个错误角度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands offered in the wrong direction.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手朝错的方向伸出。

branches.cn: 笨拙地爬

branches.en: moved awkwardly
branches.cn: 笨拙地移动

intro.cn: 后缀 -ly 构成方式副词，如 awkwardly 与 calmly。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; the base is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，词基来自日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 经受住；抵挡；抵抗；承受住压力、攻击或诱惑
definition_en: to be strong enough not to be damaged, defeated or changed by something
core_image: 狂风撞向岩石，岩石一动不动，风只好绕着走
scene: 台风过境，玻璃窗被吹得嗡嗡作响，却始终没碎。 The bridge was built to withstand winds of up to two hundred kilometres an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 withstand 是「经受住、抵挡」（第 1 个义项：强壮到不被破坏或击败）；句意为这座桥按能抵挡每小时两百公里的风速来建造。

pos.zh: 动词：经受住、抵挡、抵抗；承受得住

derivatives.zh: 不规则过去式与过去分词，义为「经受住了」
现在分词，义为「正在抵挡」
第三人称单数形式，义为「（他/它）抵挡得住」
加 -er 构成，较少用，义为「抵御者」

senses.title: To bear a force
senses.titleCN: 经受住：承受住外力而不被破坏
senses.definition: to be strong enough to bear a force without being damaged
senses.definitionCN: 强壮到能承受外力而不受损坏
senses.example: The roof is designed to withstand heavy snow.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶的设计能承受大雪。
senses.why: The word joins with, here meaning against, and stand: to stand against a force is to remain standing under it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 with（此处意为「对着」）与 stand「站立」组成：对着外力仍然站住，就是承受住它。

senses.title: To resist attack
senses.definition: to resist an attack or pressure, especially military or verbal
senses.definitionCN: 抵御攻击或压力，尤指军事或言辞上的
senses.example: The walls withstood the siege for three months.
senses.exampleCN: 城墙在围攻下坚持了三个月。
senses.why: The standing image turns defensive: the one who stands does not fall and does not yield.
senses.whyCN: 「站」的意象转为防御性的：站住的人既不倒，也不退。

senses.title: To survive a test of time
senses.titleCN: 经受住考验：历时长久而不坏
senses.definition: to remain in good condition or in force over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 长期保持良好状态或仍然有效
senses.example: Few ideas withstand the test of time.
senses.exampleCN: 能经受住时间考验的想法并不多。
senses.why: Time is treated as a force like wind or water: the metaphor of physical resistance is extended to endurance.
senses.whyCN: 时间被当成风与水那样的外力：物理抵抗的比喻延伸为持久。

senses.title: To resist temptation
senses.titleCN: 抵挡诱惑：不被人心所动
senses.definition: to refuse to give in to a desire or an influence
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝向欲望或影响屈服
senses.example: He withstood the temptation to open the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 他抵住了拆开那封信的诱惑。
senses.why: Here nothing physical presses: what must be stood against is one's own wish, and the same verb covers both.
senses.whyCN: 此处并无实体在压迫：需要顶住的是自己的意愿，而同一个动词兼管两者。

senses.title: To endure hardship
senses.definition: to get through a difficult period without being broken by it
senses.definitionCN: 度过艰难时期而未被击垮
senses.example: The family withstood months of cold and hunger.
senses.exampleCN: 这一家人熬过了数月的寒冷与饥饿。
senses.why: The older sense of standing firm shades into endurance: not just not falling, but keeping on.
senses.whyCN: 「站稳」的旧义滑向「忍受」：不只是不倒，还要继续撑下去。

intro.en: Withstand is an Old English compound of with, here meaning against, and stand: to stand against something.
intro.cn: withstand 是古英语复合词，由 with（此处意为「对着、反对」）与 stand「站」构成：对着某物站住。

items.en: Widstandan meant 'to stand against, to oppose, to resist', with wid- carrying the hostile sense of against.
items.cn: 古英语 widstandan 意为「对着站、反对、抵抗」，其中 wid- 带「对着、敌对」之义。

items.en: The prefix with- once meant against in many verbs, as in withhold and withdraw.
items.cn: 前缀 with- 曾在一大批动词中表示「对抗」，如 withhold、withdraw。

items.en: The verb belongs to an old group of compounds whose first element meant against or away.
items.cn: 这个词属于一组古老的复合词，其第一个成分意为「对着」或「离开」。

items.en: Withstonden kept both the physical sense of bearing a force and the moral sense of resisting.
items.cn: 中古英语 withstonden 同时保留「承受外力」的物理义与「抗拒」的道德义。

items.en: The past form withstood was fixed by analogy with stood, and the verb spread to tests of weather, time and desire.
items.cn: 过去式 withstood 依 stood 类推而定形，动词后来扩展到天气、时间与欲望的考验。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other with- compounds and the stand family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of resisting and enduring.
note.cn: 形近组收其他 with- 复合词与 stand 一族；近义组收表示抵抗与忍耐的动词。

entries.definition: To hold something back; another with- compound.
entries.definitionCN: 同前缀复合词，义为「扣住、不给」。

entries.definition: To draw back or take out; the prefix again means away.
entries.definitionCN: 同前缀复合词，义为「撤退、取出」。

entries.definition: To grasp a meaning; formed with stand but unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 形近词，义为「理解」，也由 stand 构成但来源不同。

entries.definition: The irregular past tense and past participle.
entries.definitionCN: 派生形式，即不规则过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: To push back against something, from Latin; broader and more neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抵抗」，源自拉丁语，范围更广、更中性。

entries.definition: To bear pain or hardship over time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「忍受」，强调长时间承受痛苦与艰苦。

entries.definition: To carry or put up with something; the plain everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承受」，最平实的日常用词。

entries.definition: To come through something and still exist.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「幸存」，强调事后仍然存在。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English compound with-stand and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语复合词 with-stand，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Withstand is with in its old sense of against plus stand: to stand against.
normal.cn: withstand 就是取 with 的旧义「对着」加 stand：对着站住。

normal.en: The prefix with- also means against in withhold and withdraw.
normal.cn: 前缀 with- 在 withhold、withdraw 中也表示「对抗」。

normal.en: Withstand the test of time is the most common abstract use.
normal.cn: withstand the test of time 是最常见的抽象用法。

normal.en: The past tense is withstood, built on stood.
normal.cn: 过去式是 withstood，由 stood 类推而来。

normal.en: Buildings and bridges are described as built to withstand storms.
normal.cn: 建筑与桥梁常说 built to withstand storms。

abstract.en: Picture a rock facing a gale: the wind must go around it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块迎风的岩石：风只能绕过去。

abstract.en: The word measures strength by what remains after the force has passed.
abstract.cn: 这个词用外力过后剩下什么来衡量强度。

abstract.en: Standing is the whole idea: whatever does not fall has withstood.
abstract.cn: 「站着」就是全部：没有倒下的，就是经受住了。

examples.en: The tower has withstood earthquakes for six hundred years.
examples.cn: 这座塔经受住了六百年来的地震。

examples.en: These plants can withstand long periods without rain.
examples.cn: 这些植物能耐受长时间无雨。

examples.en: She withstood pressure from every side and kept her decision.
examples.cn: 她顶住了各方的压力，坚持了自己的决定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为着站」——为着站住不倒，就得抵住风暴：经受住

root: 古英语 wid「对着、反对」+ standan「站」→ widstandan → 英语 withstand；同族有 withstood、withhold、withdraw。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of withstand all rest on standing against something: a physical force, an attack, the wear of time, a temptation, and a stretch of hardship.
sensesIntro.cn: withstand 的五个义项都建立在「对着站住」上：物理外力、攻击、时间磨损、诱惑，以及一段艰苦。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rock in a gale, unmoved while the wind bends around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：狂风中的岩石，纹丝不动，风只能绕行。

branches.en: THE FORCE: roofs and bridges built to carry snow and wind.
branches.cn: 外力线：为承受雪与风而建的屋顶、桥梁。

branches.en: THE ATTACK: walls that hold against a siege.
branches.cn: 攻击线：围城之下仍不倒的城墙。

branches.en: THE TIME: ideas that withstand the test of time.
branches.cn: 时间线：经受住时间考验的想法。

branches.en: THE DESIRE: the temptation not opened.
branches.cn: 欲望线：抵住而没有拆开的诱惑。

branches.en: THE HARDSHIP: a family that gets through cold and hunger.
branches.cn: 艰苦线：熬过寒冷与饥饿的一家人。

intro.en: Withstand is a native compound: the old prefix with- meaning against plus the strong verb stand.
intro.cn: withstand 是本族复合词：旧前缀 with-（意为「对抗」）加强动词 stand。

latinIntro.en: With- and stand are both Germanic; the Latin words for resisting, resistere and sustinere, are unrelated in form.
latinIntro.cn: with- 与 stand 都属日耳曼语；拉丁语表示抵抗的 resistere、sustinere 在形态上与之无关。

items.exampleCN: 它在 withstand、withhold 中带对抗义。

items.example: It is the base verb of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个复合词的本动词。

items.example: It forms the past tense withstood.
It builds resist, the Latin-side near synonym.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 resist，即拉丁系的近义词。

items.example: It builds sustain, a Latin cousin in meaning.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 sustain，是语义上的拉丁表亲。

definition_zh: 零；零度；无；微不足道的人
definition_en: the number that comes before one, the point marked zero on a scale, or nothing at all
core_image: 温度计上那条细细的刻度线，左边是负数，右边是正数
scene: 夜里降温，院子里的水盆结了一层薄冰，气温表停在最低那道线上。 The temperature fell to zero just after midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 zero 是「零度」（第 2 个义项：刻度上的零点）；句意为刚过午夜气温就降到了零度。温度计上那条细细的刻度线，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: zero 的另一种复数形式，义为「零；若干个零」
由 zero 加 -th 构成，义为「第零的（序列中的第一个）」

senses.title: The number before one
senses.definition: the number that comes before one, written as 0, and used to show that there is none of something
senses.definitionCN: 排在 1 之前的数，写作 0，用来表示某物一点也没有
senses.example: Write a zero at the end of the number and the value grows ten times.
senses.exampleCN: 在数字末尾添一个零，数值就扩大十倍。
senses.why: The word came from Arabic through Italian, where it named the empty place in a written number.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经意大利语来自阿拉伯语，在那里它指数字书写中空出来的那一位。

senses.title: The mark on a scale
senses.definition: the point marked zero on a scale of temperature or measurement, from which values go up or down
senses.definitionCN: 温度或测量刻度上的零点，数值由此向上或向下
senses.example: The temperature fell to zero just after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 刚过午夜气温就降到了零度。
senses.why: A number that means nothing becomes a useful fixed point, so scales borrow it as their starting line.
senses.whyCN: 一个表示「无」的数成了好用的固定点，于是各种刻度都借它当起始线。

senses.title: Nothing at all
senses.definition: used as an adjective or noun to mean no amount whatever, as in zero chance
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词或名词，表示一点也没有，如 zero chance
senses.example: There is zero chance of rain before evening.
senses.exampleCN: 傍晚前下雨的可能性为零。
senses.why: Since zero states the absence of amount, it fits any noun where none of something exists.
senses.whyCN: 既然零表示数量的空缺，它就能配任何「一点也没有」的名词。

senses.title: The person of no importance
senses.definition: an unimportant or unsuccessful person, used in informal speech as an insult
senses.definitionCN: 不重要或没成就的人，口语中用作贬称
senses.example: He called himself a zero after losing the match.
senses.exampleCN: 输掉比赛后他自称是个废物。
senses.why: If zero means nothing, then a person worth nothing is called a zero by the same logic.
senses.whyCN: 既然零意味着什么都不是，按同样的逻辑，毫无价值的人就被叫作零。

senses.title: The starting point
senses.definition: the lowest or first point from which something is counted or measured
senses.definitionCN: 计数或测量所依据的最低点或最初点
senses.example: They had to build the whole system from zero.
senses.exampleCN: 他们不得不从零开始搭整套系统。
senses.why: A line value everyone shares becomes a place to start, so zero also names a beginning.
senses.whyCN: 一条人人共有的数值线就成了起点，于是零也指开端。

intro.en: Zero came into English through Italian and French from Arabic ṣifr, which first meant empty.
intro.cn: zero 经意大利语与法语进入英语，源自阿拉伯语 ṣifr，最初意为「空的」。

items.en: ṣifr meant empty and was used for the empty place in a written numeral.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 ṣifr 意为「空的」，用来指数字书写中空出来的那一位。

items.en: Scholars translated the Arabic word as zephirum or cifra, and the empty place became a sign.
items.cn: 学者把阿拉伯语译作 zephirum 或 cifra，那个空位成了一个符号。

items.en: zefiro and zero named both the sign and the number it stood for.
items.cn: 意大利语 zefiro 与 zero 既指标记也指它所代表的数。

items.en: The form passed into French as zéro before reaching English.
items.cn: 这一形式先成为法语 zéro，再进入英语。

items.en: English took zero in the seventeenth century, and it later spread to temperature scales and figures of speech.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 zero，后来扩用到温度刻度与各种说法中。

note.en: Zero is compared with the other words for nothing and with the number words around it.
note.cn: zero 与其它表示「无」的词以及相邻的数词作对照。

entries.definition: a code or a written figure, from the same word
entries.definitionCN: 同一阿拉伯语来源，密码，数字

entries.definition: a soft gentle wind, unrelated in origin
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，和风，词源不同

entries.definition: the ordinal form, as in zeroth law
entries.definitionCN: 同根序数词，如 zeroth law

entries.definition: no thing at all
zero, used in scores and records
entries.definitionCN: 近义，比分与记录里的零

entries.definition: the number after zero

normalIntro.en: The word travelled from an Arabic word for empty into English, keeping the idea of a gap.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从阿拉伯语中表示「空」的词一路走进英语，保留了空位的观念。

normal.en: Write a zero after a number and you fill a place that adds a power of ten.
normal.cn: 在数后添零就是占了空位，却把数值提高十倍。

normal.en: Its cousin cipher keeps the old meaning of a written sign as well as a code.
normal.cn: 同源的 cipher 既保留「书写符号」也指密码。

normal.en: Zero tolerance and zero chance show the adjective use meaning none at all.
normal.cn: zero tolerance 与 zero chance 显示了「毫无」的形容用法。

normal.en: Below zero and zero degrees belong to the temperature scale, the fixed point of measuring.
normal.cn: below zero 与 zero degrees 属于温度刻度，是测量的固定点。

normal.en: The plural can be zeros or zeroes, and both appear in print.
normal.cn: 复数可写 zeros 或 zeroes，两种都在书面上出现。

abstract.en: Picture a thin line on a thermometer with ice on one side and steam on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象温度计上一条细线，一边是冰，一边是蒸汽。

abstract.en: Picture an empty chair in a classroom where a pupil should be sitting.
abstract.cn: 想象教室里本该坐人的一张空椅。

abstract.en: Picture a row of digits with one empty slot glowing in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一排数字，中间有一格空位发着光。

examples.en: The temperature fell to zero just after midnight.
examples.cn: 刚过午夜气温就降到了零度。

examples.en: There is zero chance of rain before evening.
examples.cn: 傍晚前下雨的可能性为零。

examples.en: They had to build the whole system from zero.
examples.cn: 他们不得不从零开始搭整套系统。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「走喽」——跑完最后一圈记分牌上只剩一个圆圈，人也「走喽」，场上什么也不剩，这个圆圈就是 zero。

root: 经意大利语、法语借自阿拉伯语 ṣifr（空的、空位），中世纪拉丁语作 zephirum、cifra；与 cipher 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The sign for an empty place becomes a number, then a fixed point on scales, a total absence, and a word for someone worth nothing.
sensesIntro.cn: 表示空位的符号先成为数字，再成为刻度上的固定点、彻底的「无」，最后指毫无价值的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the line on a scale where nothing is counted
core.cn: 核心意象：刻度上什么都不计的那条线

branches.en: The number grew out of a written gap for an empty place.
branches.cn: 数字是从书写中表示空位的空格长出来的。

branches.en: Scales take that number as a fixed reference line.
branches.cn: 各种刻度把这个数当作固定参照线。

branches.en: Saying nobody has any of something uses the same zero.
branches.cn: 说某人毫无某物也用同一个零。

branches.en: A person worth nothing is called by the number that means nothing.
branches.cn: 毫无价值的人就用表示「无」的数来称。

branches.en: The shared line also becomes the place to begin.
branches.cn: 这条共有的线也成了开始的起点。

intro.en: Zero forms a regular plural and a rare ordinal, and appears in many fixed phrases.
intro.cn: zero 有规则的复数与少见的序数形式，并出现在许多固定说法中。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form cifra, taken from Arabic, is the ancestor of both zero and cipher.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 cifra 借自阿拉伯语，既是 zero 也是 cipher 的祖先。

items.example: Add two zeros to the figure.
items.exampleCN: 在这个数字后加两个零。

items.meaning: forming zeroes, used in British style

items.example: The zeroth law comes before the first.
items.exampleCN: 第零定律排在第一条之前。

items.example: Latin cifra gives both zero and cipher.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 cifra 同时给出 zero 与 cipher。

items.example: Arabic sifr passed into many languages.
items.exampleCN: 阿拉伯语 sifr 流入许多语言。

items.example: It stayed below zero all week.

items.meaning: no acceptance of an offence at all
items.example: The school has zero tolerance for cheating.

latinEntries.meaning: the empty place in a numeral

definition_en: to release a substance, a person or a duty, or the substance that is released
core_image: 水管口喷出一股白水，落在石头上溅起一片雾
scene: 工厂的管子对着河面，水色发灰，岸边浮着一层沫。 The factory was fined for discharging waste into the river.
sceneCN: 这里 discharging 指「排放」（第 1 个义项：把液体或气体排出）；句意是这家工厂因向河里排放废物被罚款。

senses.title: To let a substance flow out
senses.definition: to release liquid, gas or waste into the environment
senses.definitionCN: 把液体、气体或废物排到环境里
senses.example: The factory was fined for discharging waste into the river.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂因向河里排放废物被罚款。
senses.why: The pipe does not ask the river whether it wants the water.
senses.whyCN: 管子不问河水要不要这些水，只管往外放。

senses.title: To allow someone to leave
senses.definition: to allow a patient, soldier or prisoner to leave officially
senses.definitionCN: 正式允许病人、军人或囚犯离开
senses.example: She was discharged from hospital on Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 她周五出院了。
senses.why: The door opens only when someone with authority says it may.
senses.whyCN: 那扇门，只有在有权的人说可以时才会开。

senses.title: To carry out a duty or pay a debt
senses.definition: to perform a duty fully or to pay what is owed
senses.definitionCN: 把职责做到底，或把欠的还清
senses.example: He discharged his duties without complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 他毫无怨言地履行了职责。
senses.why: A load is set down only when nothing is left on it.
senses.whyCN: 只有什么都不剩了，肩上的担子才算卸下。

intro.en: Discharge came from Old French deschargier, to unload, built on chargier, to load, and Latin carrus, a cart.
intro.cn: discharge 来自古法语 deschargier（卸货），词基 chargier 意为装载，更早是拉丁语 carrus（车）。

items.en: Carrus named a four-wheeled cart.
items.cn: carrus 指四轮货车。

items.en: Carricare meant to load a cart or a beast.
items.cn: carricare 指往车上或牲口背上装货。

items.en: Chargier meant to load, and deschargier meant to unload.
items.cn: chargier 指装载，deschargier 指卸下。

items.en: Discharge first meant to unload goods or a ship.
items.cn: discharge 最初指卸货或卸船。

items.en: The word widened to waste, patients, soldiers and duties.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到废物、病人、军人与职责。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the charge stem, while the meaning group names other kinds of letting go.
note.cn: 形近组共用 charge 这一段词干，近义组则列出其他放手的说法。

entries.definition: to load, to ask a price, or to accuse
a device that puts power into a battery
to put fresh power into a battery
to let a person or substance go free
to send out light, sound or gas
to send someone away or remove them from a job
entries.definitionCN: 让某人离开，或解除其职务

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a pipe pouring into a river to a duty finally paid in full.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从往河里灌水的管子，走到终于还清的职责。

normal.en: Dis- plus charge: the load is taken off.
normal.cn: dis- 加 charge：把担子卸下来。

normal.en: A pipe discharges; a ward discharges; a soldier is discharged.
normal.cn: 管子排放，病房放人，军人退役，都是这个词。

normal.en: To discharge a duty is to leave nothing owed.
normal.cn: 履行职责，就是把欠的都清掉。

normal.en: The river carries away what the pipe lets go.
normal.cn: 管子放出的东西，由河水带走。

normal.en: The word always means a load leaving a place.
normal.cn: 这个词始终意味着：有一份重量离开了原处。

abstract.en: Picture grey water spreading under a pipe.
abstract.cn: 想象灰水在管口下面散开。

abstract.en: Picture a hospital door opening for a walking patient.
abstract.cn: 想象病房的门为一个能走路的病人打开。

abstract.en: Picture an empty cart with its wheels still turning.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆空车，轮子还在转。

examples.en: The factory was fined for discharging waste into the river.
examples.cn: 这家工厂因向河里排放废物被罚款。

examples.en: She was discharged from hospital on Friday.
examples.cn: 她周五出院了。

examples.en: He discharged his duties without complaint.
examples.cn: 他毫无怨言地履行了职责。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discharge 记成「的士查值」：的士到站查完值就卸客，人货一起放出去。

root: 来自古法语 deschargier（卸货），由表示「去除」的 des- 加 chargier（装载）构成，更早可追到拉丁语 carrus（车）。本义是把货从车上卸下，后来引申为排出液体与气体、准许病人或军人离开，以及履行完职责、还清债务，仿佛卸下肩上的重担。

sensesIntro.en: From waste leaving a pipe, to a patient leaving a ward, to a duty leaving a person's shoulders.
sensesIntro.cn: 从离开管口的废物，到离开病房的病人，再到离开肩头的职责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pipe pouring out, and a cart standing empty.
core.cn: 核心意象：管子往外倒，车子空了下来。

chain: A DUTY IS PAID IN FULL

branches.en: The first sense is a substance let out.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是被放出来的物质。

branches.en: The second sense is a person allowed to go.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是被准许离开的人。

branches.en: The third sense is a load of duty carried to the end.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是扛到底、终于卸下的职责。

branches.en: Water and people both leave through an opening.
branches.cn: 水与人，都是从某个出口离开。

branches.en: Leaving a post and finishing a duty are two ends of one service.
branches.cn: 离开岗位与完成职责，是同一段服务的两头。

intro.en: Discharge belongs to the charge family, words about loading, cost and command.
intro.cn: discharge 属于 charge 一族，围绕装载、费用与命令。

latinIntro.en: Latin carrus, a cart, gives carricare, to load, and through French the base charge.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carrus（车）给出 carricare（装载），再经法语形成词基 charge。

items.example: The pipe discharges into the sea.
items.exampleCN: 这根管子把水排进海里。

items.meaning: to load, to ask a price, or to accuse
items.example: They charge ten pounds for the tour.

items.meaning: to ask too high a price
items.example: The taxi driver tried to overcharge us.
items.exampleCN: 出租车司机想多收我们的钱。

items.meaning: an extra amount added to a price
items.example: There is a surcharge for late payment.

items.meaning: loaded with power or filled with feeling
items.example: The room felt charged with anger.
items.exampleCN: 屋里弥漫着愤怒的紧张气氛。

items.meaning: the act of loading or supplying power
items.example: The phone is charging on the desk.

definition_zh: 轻微的；不严重的；温和的；和善的；暖和的；（味道）淡的
definition_en: not severe or harsh in degree; gentle and kind in manner; warmer than expected for the season; and soft rather than sharp in taste
core_image: 冬日午后，阳光斜照进院子，一只猫在石阶上伸了个懒腰
scene: 冬日的午后阳光斜照进院子，石阶上一点风也没有，老猫在墙根下慢慢伸了个懒腰。 The winter here is almost mild enough for the cat to sleep outdoors.
sceneCN: 这里是「天气暖和的、温和的」（第 3 个义项：天气不冷冽）；句意为这里的冬天暖和得几乎能让猫睡在户外。图中可辨识物件：斜照的阳光、石阶、伸懒腰的猫。

pos.zh: 轻微的；温和的；暖和的；味淡的

derivatives.zh: 由 mild 加 -ly 构成，义为「轻微地；温和地」
由 mild 加 -ness 构成，义为「温和；轻微」
由 mild 与 mannered 复合而成，义为「举止温和的」

senses.title: Not severe or harsh in degree
senses.definition: not strong, serious or severe, especially of illness, pain or a punishment
senses.definitionCN: 不强烈、不严重、不厉害，尤用于疾病、疼痛或惩罚
senses.example: He had a mild fever and stayed home for one day.
senses.exampleCN: 他发了低烧，在家待了一天。
senses.why: Old English milde meant gentle and merciful, so this sense measures severity by how little force is used rather than by how much there is.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 milde 意为温和、仁慈，所以这一义项是用「用力之少」来衡量严重程度，而不是看它有多少力量。

senses.title: Gentle and kind in character or manner
senses.definition: kind, gentle and not easily angry in the way someone speaks or behaves
senses.definitionCN: 说话或行事和气、温和，不轻易发怒
senses.example: Her mild reply quietened the room more than any argument could.
senses.exampleCN: 她温和的回答比任何争辩都更能让房间安静下来。
senses.why: The oldest sense was moral: milde described a person who holds back anger, and that gentleness of character is still the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思带有道德色彩：milde 形容一个人压得住怒气；这种性情上的温和至今仍是这个词的中心。

senses.title: Warmer than expected for the season
senses.definition: used of weather or a climate that is not as cold or as harsh as it could be
senses.definitionCN: 用于天气或气候，表示没有本该有的那么冷、那么严酷
senses.example: The winter here is almost mild enough for the cat to sleep outdoors.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的冬天暖和得几乎能让猫睡在户外。
senses.why: Once the word means little force, it fits weather as well, because a mild winter is simply one that uses less of winter's force.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词表示「用力很小」，它也适用于天气：一个温和的冬天，就是冬天没怎么使出它的力气。

senses.title: Not strong in taste or effect
senses.definition: having a soft, not sharp taste, or a gentle effect on the body
senses.definitionCN: 味道柔和、不刺激，或对身体作用平缓
senses.example: The cheese is mild, so it suits people who dislike sharp flavours.
senses.exampleCN: 这种奶酪味道清淡，适合不喜欢刺激口味的人。
senses.why: The same measure of low intensity transfers from pain to the tongue, so a mild cheese is one that hits the mouth with very little force.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「强度低」从疼痛转到舌头上：味道淡的奶酪，就是以很小的力气碰触口腔的那种。

intro.en: Mild goes back to Old English milde meaning gentle and merciful; it belongs to the Germanic branch and has no reliable Latin cognate.
intro.cn: mild 可追溯到古英语 milde，意为温和、仁慈；它属于日耳曼语这一支，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: The adjective is generally traced to a Germanic form meaning gentle or kind, though its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为这个形容词来自日耳曼语中表示「温和、和善」的形式，但其更早来源不确定。

items.en: Milde meant gentle, merciful and kind, and it applied to rulers, judges and ordinary people alike.
items.cn: milde 意为温和、仁慈、和善，可用于君主、法官，也可用于普通人。

items.en: Middle English mild kept the moral sense of gentleness and began to describe weather and taste as well.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mild 保留「性情温和」的道德义，并开始形容天气与味道。

items.en: Writers extended mild from people to seasons, medicines and flavours, wherever force was noticeably low.
items.cn: 文人把 mild 从人扩展到季节、药物与味道，凡是用力明显较小之处都可以用它。

items.en: Modern English uses mild most often for small degrees of illness, gentle manners, soft weather and light flavours.
items.cn: 现代英语中，mild 最常用于轻微的病、和气的举止、温和的天气与清淡的味道。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family built on mild and one word that only shares its shape; the near-meaning group collects words for gentleness, slightness and softness.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 mild 上的词族，外加一个只在字形上相近的词；近义组收表示温和、轻微与柔软的词。

entries.definition: In a gentle way, or only a little.
entries.definitionCN: 以温和的方式，或只稍微地。

entries.definition: The quality of being gentle or not severe.
A fungus that grows on damp surfaces; only the spelling is close and the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 生长在潮湿表面的霉；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Having a gentle way of behaving, built from mild and mannered.
entries.definitionCN: 举止温和的，由 mild 与 mannered 构成。

entries.definition: Soft and kind in manner, without force.
entries.definitionCN: 举止柔和、善意，不带强势。

entries.definition: Not hard or sharp, either to touch or to hear.
entries.definitionCN: 触感或听感上不硬、不刺。

entries.definition: Small in degree or amount, said of damage or change.
entries.definitionCN: 程度或数量小，用于损伤或变化。

entries.definition: Neither too much nor too little, kept within limits.
entries.definitionCN: 既不过多也不过少，保持在限度之内。

entries.definition: Mild and steady, especially of climate.

normalIntro.en: The word rests on an Old English adjective for gentleness; its family keeps returning to small force, soft weather and the kind of manner that holds anger back.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在一个意为温和的古英语形容词上，同族词反复回到「用力很小」、柔和的天气，以及压得住怒气的举止。

normal.en: Milde in Old English meant gentle and merciful, so mild begins as a moral word rather than a medical one.
normal.cn: 古英语 milde 意为温和、仁慈，所以 mild 起初属于道德词汇，而不是医学词汇。

normal.en: The word measures how little force is used, which is why a mild fever and a mild winter feel like the same idea.
normal.cn: 这个词衡量的是「用力有多小」，所以轻微发烧与温和的冬天感觉上是同一个想法。

normal.en: Milder and mildest add -er and -est, because mild is a short adjective that takes the regular comparison.
normal.cn: milder 与 mildest 分别加 -er 与 -est，因为 mild 是短形容词，走规则比较级。

normal.en: Mildly adds -ly and keeps the meaning of small force or gentle manner.
normal.cn: mildly 加 -ly，保留了「力气小」或「举止温和」的意思。

normal.en: Mildew looks close but means a mould; the two words only share a shape, not a source.
normal.cn: mildew 看上去很像，却指霉菌；两个词只共用外形，不共用来源。

abstract.en: A word for gentleness that also measures illness suggests that kindness and severity sit on one single scale.
abstract.cn: 一个既指温和又能衡量病情的词说明：善意与严重程度坐在同一把尺子上。

abstract.en: Mild weather is winter using less of its force, a picture that makes climate feel almost like a person holding back.
abstract.cn: 温和的天气就是冬天少用了些力气，这个画面让气候几乎像一个人收住了手。

abstract.en: Because mild can describe a voice, a fever and a cheese, the word quietly claims that force is what all three have in common.
abstract.cn: 因为 mild 能形容嗓音、发烧和奶酪，这个词其实在说：三者共通之处就是「力气的大小」。

examples.en: He had a mild fever and stayed home for one day.
examples.cn: 他发了低烧，在家待了一天。

examples.en: The winter here is almost mild enough for the cat to sleep outdoors.
examples.cn: 这里的冬天暖和得几乎能让猫睡在户外。

examples.en: The cheese is mild, so it suits people who dislike sharp flavours.
examples.cn: 这种奶酪味道清淡，适合不喜欢刺激口味的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迈尔德」——迈着慢步、脾气很软的人；记住 mild 是温和的、轻微的。

root: 古英语 milde（温和的、仁慈的）来自日耳曼语中表示「和善」的形式；一般认为其更早来源不确定，且没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is low force; the senses spread from a slight illness to a gentle manner, soft weather and a light taste.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「用力很小」；义项从轻微的病扩到和气的举止、柔和的天气与清淡的味道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a winter afternoon, sunlight falling across a yard, a cat stretching on the stone steps.
core.cn: 核心意象：冬日午后，阳光斜照进院子，一只猫在石阶上伸了个懒腰。

branches.en: a thermometer showing only a small rise
branches.cn: 温度计上只升了一小格

branches.en: a soft answer that ends an argument
branches.cn: 一句结束争吵的柔和回答

branches.en: a cat sleeping outside in midwinter
branches.cn: 隆冬里睡在户外的猫

branches.en: a pale cheese that does not bite the tongue
branches.cn: 一块不刺激舌头的浅色奶酪

branches.en: a nurse speaking softly about a small fever
branches.cn: 护士低声说着轻微的发热

intro.en: The word is carried by an Old English adjective of gentleness, its Middle English respelling, and English endings that build the adverb, the noun and the comparative.
intro.cn: 这个词由意为温和的古英语形容词、中古英语拼写，以及构成副词、名词与比较级的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for mild: the word belongs to the Germanic branch, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: mild 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，它属于日耳曼语这一支，因此拉丁同源部分留空。

definition_en: to make a sick person well, or a treatment that ends a disease
core_image: 一碗苦药放在床头，喝完的人第二天能下床
scene: 床头的苦药喝完了，第二天那人就能下床。 There is still no cure for that disease.
sceneCN: 这里 cure 指「疗法、治愈的手段」（第 1 个义项：能结束疾病的治疗方法）；句意是那种病至今仍没有疗法。

senses.title: Make well again
senses.definition: to make a sick person healthy again
senses.definitionCN: 使病人恢复健康
senses.example: The doctor cured him of the infection.
senses.exampleCN: 医生治好了他的感染。
senses.why: A body can be brought back to its own order.
senses.whyCN: 身体能被带回它本来的秩序。

senses.title: A treatment
senses.definition: a medicine or treatment that ends a disease
senses.definitionCN: 结束疾病的药物或疗法
senses.example: There is no cure for the common cold.
senses.exampleCN: 普通感冒没有特效疗法。
senses.why: We name the end of an illness after the thing that ends it.
senses.whyCN: 我们用结束疾病的东西，来称呼疾病的终结。

senses.title: Preserve with salt
senses.definition: to treat food with salt or smoke so that it keeps
senses.definitionCN: 用盐或烟处理食物以便保存
senses.example: They cure the meat in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在冬天腌肉。
senses.why: Salt pulls water out so that nothing spoils.
senses.whyCN: 盐把水抽走，东西就不坏了。

intro.en: Cure comes from Latin cura, care, and curare, to care for a person, through Old French curer.
intro.cn: cure 源自拉丁语 cura（关心、照料）与 curare（照看），经古法语 curer 进入英语。

items.en: Cura meant care and concern.
items.cn: cura 意为关心与挂念。

items.en: Curare meant to take care of a person.
items.cn: curare 意为照看一个人。

items.en: Curer meant to clean or to heal.
items.cn: curer 意为清理或治愈。

items.en: Cure meant to restore a person to health.
items.cn: cure 指使人恢复健康。

items.en: A cure also named the treatment itself.
items.cn: cure 也指治疗手段本身。

items.en: It extended to preserving meat with salt.
items.cn: 它扩展到用盐保存肉类。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cu- opening, and the meaning group names other words for healing and fixing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cu- 开头，近义组列出其他治愈与解决的说法。

to hold something back
the central part of something

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a bitter bowl and end with salt on winter meat.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一碗苦药开始，落到冬天肉上的盐。

normal.en: Cure began as care, not as medicine.
normal.cn: cure 最初是照料，不是药。

normal.en: A doctor cares for a body until it finds its order.
normal.cn: 医生照料身体，直到它找回秩序。

normal.en: The cold has no cure, only time.
normal.cn: 感冒没有药，只有时间。

normal.en: Salt cures meat by taking its water away.
normal.cn: 盐靠夺走水来腌肉。

normal.en: One word covers healing a man and keeping a ham.
normal.cn: 一个词既管治好一个人，也管保住一条火腿。

abstract.cn: 想象床头柜上一勺深色药。

abstract.en: Picture a fever line falling on a chart.
abstract.cn: 想象图上的发烧曲线往下走。

abstract.en: Picture white salt rubbed into red meat.
abstract.cn: 想象白盐揉进红肉里。

examples.cn: 这种新药也许能治好这种病。

examples.cn: 他们没找到治这种高烧的疗法。

examples.en: The fish is cured with salt and smoke.
examples.cn: 这鱼用盐和烟腌制。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cure 记成「照料」：拉丁语 cura 是关心，用心照料到病好，就是治愈。

root: 源自拉丁语 cura（关心、照料），动词 curare 意为照看病人，经古法语 curer 进入英语；本义是照料，后指治愈、疗法，也指用盐保存食物。

sensesIntro.en: From caring for a patient, to ending a disease, to preserving food.
sensesIntro.cn: 从照看病人，到结束疾病，再到保存食物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bitter bowl of medicine beside a sickbed.
core.cn: 核心意象：病床边一碗苦药。

branches.en: Care brings the body back to health.
branches.cn: 照料把身体带回健康。

branches.en: The thing that ends an illness is called a cure.
branches.cn: 结束疾病的东西被称为疗法。

branches.en: Salt does for meat what care does for a patient.
branches.cn: 盐对肉做的事，就像照料对病人做的事。

branches.en: The act of caring and the drug both carry the name.

branches.en: Ending sickness and keeping food are both cures.
branches.cn: 结束疾病与保存食物都叫 cure。

intro.en: Cure forms words for healing, for what can and cannot be healed, and for the care of feet.
intro.cn: cure 组成一族词，关于治愈、能否治愈，以及足部护理。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cura, care, is the root behind cure, curable, and incurable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cura（照料）是 cure、curable 与 incurable 背后的根。

definition_en: a vehicle designed to travel in space, crewed or unmanned
core_image: 银白色的航天器在地球弧线之上缓缓展开太阳能板
scene: 这艘航天器成功进入了轨道。 The spacecraft entered orbit successfully.

intro.en: Spacecraft joins space with craft, an old word for skill and a vessel.
intro.cn: spacecraft 由 space 与 craft 组合，craft 古义为技艺，也指船只。

items.en: Spacecraft was coined for vehicles in space.

items.en: It covered both crewed ships and unmanned probes.

note.en: Spacecraft is compared with look-alike compounds and space vehicles.

definition_en: the part of the face below the mouth and above the neck
core_image: 抬起下巴时露出的一道侧面轮廓
scene: 摄影师让那人把头抬高一点。 He rested his chin on his hand and looked out of the window.
sceneCN: 这里 chin 指「下巴」（第 1 个义项：嘴下方的面部部位）；句意是他用手托着下巴望向窗外。

derivatives.zh: 下巴不明显的；意志薄弱的

senses.title: The part below the mouth
senses.definition: the part of the face that lies below the mouth and above the neck
senses.definitionCN: 位于嘴下方、颈部上方的面部部位
senses.example: He cut his chin while shaving.
senses.exampleCN: 他刮胡子时刮伤了下巴。
senses.why: The Old English word named the lower jaw, and the sense has stayed bodily and stable.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词指下颌，这一义项始终是身体部位且非常稳定。

senses.title: Courage to take a blow
senses.definition: the strength to accept a hard blow or criticism without giving up
senses.definitionCN: 承受重击或批评而不放弃的韧劲
senses.example: She took the bad news on the chin and kept working.
senses.exampleCN: 她默默承受了坏消息，继续工作。
senses.why: A punch lands on the chin, so the word came to stand for enduring a hit.
senses.whyCN: 拳头常打在下巴上，于是这个词被用来表示承受一击。

intro.en: Chin is an old Germanic word for the lower jaw that English has never replaced.
intro.cn: chin 是一个古老的日耳曼语词，指下颌，英语从未换掉它。

items.en: Kinnuz named the jaw or the chin.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 kinnuz 指颌或下巴。

items.en: Cin named the lower jaw and the chin.
items.cn: 古英语 cin 指下颌与下巴。

items.en: Chin settled as the everyday word for the feature.
items.cn: 中古英语 chin 定型为这个部位的日常词。

items.en: Sports talk gave chin the sense of taking a punch.
items.cn: 体育谈话让 chin 带上「挨拳」的意思。

items.en: Chin covers the body part and a group of courage idioms.
items.cn: 如今 chin 既指身体部位，也构成一组表示韧劲的习语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- and short i, while the meaning group names the lower face.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch- 与短元音 i，近义组列出面部下方的部位。

the side of the face below the eye
having little width or fat
either of the bones that hold the teeth

the outline of the lower jaw

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the jaw relatives, the chin up idiom and the double chin picture.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用颌部相关词、chin up 习语以及双下巴的画面。

normal.en: Chin and jaw sit side by side: the chin is the front point, the jaw the whole bone.
normal.cn: chin 与 jaw 相邻：chin 是前面的尖角，jaw 是整块骨。

normal.en: Keep your chin up: lift the head and the mood rises with it.
normal.cn: keep your chin up：把头抬起，心情也跟着上去。

normal.en: A double chin is a second curve under the first.
normal.cn: 双下巴就是第一道曲线下面又多出一道。

normal.en: Take it on the chin means to accept a hit without complaining.
normal.cn: take it on the chin 意为挨了打也不抱怨。

normal.en: The plural chins is regular, though the feature usually appears once.
normal.cn: 复数 chins 变化规则，尽管这个部位通常只有一个。

abstract.en: Picture a boxer lifting his head after a hard round.

examples.en: She rested her chin on her folded hands.
examples.cn: 她把下巴搁在交叠的手上。

examples.en: He took the failure on the chin and tried again.
examples.cn: 他默默承受失败，又重新尝试。

dict_mnemonic.text: chin 和 cheek 都在脸上：cheek 在脸侧，chin 在脸的最下端。

root: 源自日耳曼语 kinnuz（颌、下巴），古英语作 cin，中古英语定型为 chin。

sensesIntro.en: The bodily feature is the literal sense, and the place where a punch lands gives the sense of endurance.
sensesIntro.cn: 面部部位是字面义，而拳头落下的位置给出「承受」的义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the small point at the bottom of a face.

branches.en: The body sense names the feature itself.

branches.en: A double chin is described with the same word.

branches.en: Both senses are tied to the same small area.

branches.en: Taking it on the chin means showing no complaint.

intro.en: Chin is a short stem with only a few derived forms.
intro.cn: chin 是个短词干，派生形式不多。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, with no Latin ancestor for this everyday word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属日耳曼语，这个日常词没有拉丁语祖先。

definition_en: to place something in a particular position or context

senses.whyCN: 这是把事物放在地面上的字面义项。
